question: A 55-year-old patient presenting for the first time with a 'worst headache of life' reaching peak intensity in under 60 seconds can be diagnosed as migraine without aura if the neurological examination is entirely normal.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. A thunderclap headache ('worst headache of life', reaching maximum severity in <60 seconds) is a SNNOOP10 red flag. A normal neurological examination does NOT exclude SAH — CT head (and if negative, LP ≥12 hours) is mandatory before attributing the headache to any primary disorder.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. A thunderclap headache in a new presenter, regardless of normal neurological examination, mandates urgent CT head to exclude subarachnoid haemorrhage. Normal neurology does NOT rule out SAH; the examination is normal in over 50% of SAH cases at first presentation.
